newsitem.title: MOROCCO: Commerzbank to invest $100 mln in Morocco.
newsitem.headline: Commerzbank to invest $100 mln in Morocco.

text.p: Germany's Commerzbank AG will invest $100 million in Morocco's leading Banque Marocaine du Commerce Exterieur, Trade Minister Driss Jettou said on Tuesday evening.

Addressing a group of German and Moroccan businessmen on the occasion of the inauguration of a German chamber of commerce in Morocco's financial centre of Casablanca, Jettou said: "The Commerzbank plans to expand its activity in Morocco by investing $100 million in BMCE bank."
The investment will be finalised during an official ceremony on April 12, a Moroccan senior official said.
Earlier, German Minister of Economy Guenter Rexrodt said the new chamber of commerce, the 75th German trade office abroad, was intended to boost "business and exchanges between Germany and Morocco."
Rexrodt, who held talks on Tuesday in Rabat with Moroccan ministers of finance and trade, said the two countries should further reinforce their trade cooperation and investments.
"Commerzbank investment will be the first biggest investment devoted by Germany to Moroccan private sector in decades," the senior official added.
Last month Commerzbank announced a plan to increase its holding to 10 percent from 1.6 percent in the capital of Morocco's BMCE.
"The operation can be considered as a strategic investment which underlines the German institution's confidence in the future of the privatised BMCE," the German bank said in a statement.
Commerzbank had a 1.6 percent holding in the Moroccan bank just after its privatisation in May 1995 and before its latest move to increase its involvement, the statement said.
The BMCE's capital stands at 1.44 billion dirhams divided into 14.4 million shares of 100 dirhams nominal value.

In its latest consolidated results, BMCE showed a rise in net profits to 365.7 million dirhams ($39.7 million) in 1996 from 301 million dirhams the year before. The results included business in Morocco, at the bank's Paris agency and in the Tangier free zone in northern Morocco.
Turnover in Morocco last year rose to 2.43 billion dirhams from 2.23 billion dirhams in 1995. It gave no consolidated turnover figure.

Early in 1996, the bank increased its capital to 1.4 billion dirhams, through incorporation of reserves, a share distribution of two new shares for seven, and a $60 million international issue of Global Depository Receipts.
The stock was last traded at 616 dirhams per share.
